transcript: 20 Sided Tavern may be the most surprising show I've seen all year. I was invited to Twenty Sided Tavern and I had no idea what it was about. I had never heard of this show before. I just know Dungeons and Dragons. I've never personally played, but I have played similar games like Pathfinder. The Dungeons and Dragons themed show was intriguing to me, so I went into this completely and utterly blind. I was shocked from the moment I stepped into the building. But what was most surprising to me is I did not realize how interactive this show is. 20 Sided Tavern is essentially a D D game that is played live on stage. You have three actors that go through a quest. There's a Dungeon Master, there's a Dungeon Master's assistant. You do not have to be familiar with D D in order to enjoy this. They do explain everything to you in the intro, and the game that they're playing on the stage has, like, specific rules that they're following, so it's very, very easy to follow even if you are not a D D player. But the entire show has an interactive element that encourages you to use your phone the entire show. As you enter the theater, in your playbill, you are given an item that divides you into the red team, the blue team, or the green team, depending on which player you are primarily following. And similar to like a jackbox Game. There is an interactive element on your phone where you can answer polls to decide, like, who the actors are playing, as there's many games throughout. Now, I will say that my phone stopped interacting with the online interface about halfway through the show. This didn't ruin the show for me at all, but it did take away a big piece piece of that, which was kind of a bummer. But even without that phone element, I was having a blast. And because so much of it is decided by the audience, and like a D&D game, it is very improvised, this show is different. Basically, every time you go, there's different characters that you can get. Because of that, and because you're using your phone, they allow you to take photos and video of the show itself. Twenty Sided Tavern is essentially changing how we interact with theater, and I loved every second of it.
